mechanism_inventory: missing invariant enforcement (bounds / length / sum / cap)
access-control mismatch — receiveFromBridge is public and unguarded
victim accounting direction (who gains vs who loses)
external-call failure / DoS (unhandled revert, gas, lock)
value exceeds a logical / economic bound (e.g. a fee or ratio > 100%, a count > a documented cap)

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: receiveFromBridge is declared `public` with no access-control modifier, caller whitelist, or bridge-adapter authentication. Any EOA or contract can call it directly, supplying arbitrary swapInstructions, target, paymentOperator, payload, and refund. This is the same internal entry point used after a legitimate cross-chain bridge delivery, so it triggers _swapAndExecute with fully attacker-controlled parameters.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged EOA or contract that has pre-approved UTB to spend tokens (or that can supply native value). The attacker supplies crafted swapInstructions pointing to a swapperId that simply passes through a token already held by UTB (e.g., leftover approved token or dust), sets target/paymentOperator to drain the executor or cause UTB to approve an attacker address, and sets refund to themselves.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker calls receiveFromBridge(postBridge, target, paymentOperator, payload, refund) directly from an EOA with no privileged setup. 2. UTB calls _swapAndExecute, which calls performSwap with attacker-supplied swapInstructions. 3. performSwap reads swappers[swapInstructions.swapperId] — if the swapper is a pass-through or the attacker controls swapperId, arbitrary tokenOut/amountOut can be returned. 4. _swapAndExecute then calls IERC20(tokenOut).approve(address(executor), amountOut) or executor.execute{value:amountOut} with attacker-supplied target and payload. 5. executor.execute executes the attacker-supplied payload against the attacker-supplied target — enabling arbitrary contract calls at UTB's expense, theft of tokens in executor, or griefing of legitimate cross-chain deliveries.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Users whose tokens are held/approved by UTB or the executor at settlement time, and the protocol itself (integrity of bridge receipt routing).
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker who can redirect execution or extract tokens.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Direct access-control gap with no guard whatsoever on a function that is the cross-chain bridge receive entry point. Any attacker can invoke it permissionlessly. Different actor (bridge adapter) and authorization path than the fee-bypass mechanism. Cannot be rejected — no guard proven present in source.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In the retrieveAndCollectFees modifier, when fees.feeToken != address(0), the fee amount is pulled from msg.sender via transferFrom and approved to feeCollector, but there is no signature verification that the fee structure is authentic before the token transfer. More critically, the modifier is skipped entirely (the body still runs — `_` executes) if feeCollector == address(0). This means if the feeCollector has not been set, swapAndExecute executes without collecting any fees and without verifying the signature.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any caller of swapAndExecute when feeCollector is address(0) (unset or zeroed). Alternatively an attacker who passes fees.feeAmount=0 when feeCollector is unset — zero cost execution.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. If feeCollector == address(0): attacker calls swapAndExecute with fees.feeAmount=0 and arbitrary signature bytes. The modifier body is skipped (only `_` runs). No fees paid. 2. The swap and execute proceed at zero cost, potentially draining protocol-subsidized liquidity or bypassing rate-limit/fee controls.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol fee revenue; if the fee was meant to be a rate-limit or anti-spam mechanism, all those protections are bypassed.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker avoids fee payment; can spam or extract value at zero protocol cost.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Affects a different state variable (feeCollector, fees.feeAmount) and a different authorization path (fee collection integrity) than the receiveFromBridge access-control gap. The fee bypass is permissionless when feeCollector is unset. Source clearly shows the entire fee block is inside `if (address(feeCollector) != address(0))` with no fallback enforcement.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Executor arbitrary payload execution — attacker-supplied `payload` and `target` in _swapAndExecute/receiveFromBridge allow execution of arbitrary calldata against any contract.
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: _swapAndExecute passes attacker-controlled `target`, `paymentOperator`, `payload` directly to executor.execute() with no validation in UTB.sol. IUTBExecutor is an interface — its implementation is not in scope.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does UTB's executor implementation whitelist targets, validate payloads, or restrict callers? If not, this is a direct arbitrary-execution vulnerability compounding the receiveFromBridge access-control gap.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Any protocol or user whose funds can be targeted by the executor.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker who can redirect executor calls.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Stale or mismatched amountOut passed to executor — performSwap returns amountOut from the swapper; if a rogue swapper is registered it could return inflated amountOut while delivering fewer tokens.
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: swappers[swapInstructions.swapperId] is looked up from a mapping; receiveFromBridge is unguarded so attacker supplies swapperId directly.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether all registered swappers are trusted/vetted. Runtime behavior of specific swappers needed.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: UTB / executor if amountOut is inflated and ETH/tokens sent exceed actual balance.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker if executor forwards more than received.

rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: registerSwapper and registerBridge are both gated by `onlyOwner`. No path in swapAndExecute or _swapAndExecute deletes or overwrites these mappings.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: No user-accessible function can delete or overwrite the registries.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: Wrong lifecycle ordering within swapAndExecute itself
rejected_mechanisms.claimed_locus: performSwap return values used before swap completes
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: performSwap is synchronous; tokenOut and amountOut are settled before executor.execute is called.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Attacker can redirect swap output and executor payment via unguarded receiveFromBridge; can bypass fees when feeCollector unset.
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Fee bypass allows execution at zero protocol cost.
impact_direction.victim_loses: Users whose tokens are approved to UTB/executor at settlement; protocol fee revenue and bridge receipt integrity.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Cross-chain bridge authorization invariant: receiveFromBridge intended only for trusted bridge adapters but permissionlessly callable. Fee invariant: fees bypassable when feeCollector unset.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: receiveFromBridge exploit requires no privileged setup, no admin role, no timing; impact not dust.

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: access-control gap on receiveFromBridge + fee-bypass selected; executor arbitrary-payload scope and swapper amountOut inflation unresolved
